questions.question: Who among the following defeated Harshavardhana when he invaded the Chalukya kingdom in the Deccan?
questions.solution:
• Victor: Pulakesin II
  • Context: The Chalukya king stopped the southward expansion of Emperor Harshavardhana on the banks of the Narmada River.

questions.question: During the rule of which dynasty were Nalanda and Vikramashila universities founded?
questions.solution:
• Dynasty: The Palas
  • Education: Dharmapala founded Vikramashila, and the Palas were great patrons of Mahayana Buddhism.

questions.question: On 21 October 1943, Subhash Chandra Bose proclaimed the formation of the Provisional Government of Free India in ______.
questions.solution:
• City: Singapore
  • Government: Known as 'Azad Hind', it was supported by the Axis powers during World War II.

questions.question: The Mesopotamians wrote on tablets made of:
questions.solution:
• Material: Clay
  • Writing: They used a stylus to press wedge-shaped (Cuneiform) symbols into wet clay tablets, which were then baked.

questions.question: The Poona Pact of 1932 was an agreement between Mahatma Gandhi and ______.
questions.solution:
• Parties: Mahatma Gandhi and B.R. Ambedkar
  • Outcome: It secured reserved seats for the depressed classes in provincial legislatures instead of separate electorates.

questions.question: King Ajatashatru was a ruler of the ______ dynasty.
questions.solution:
• Dynasty: Haryanka
  • Fact: Ajatashatru was the son of Bimbisara and is famous for convening the First Buddhist Council.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about the ‘Gotra’ practice in ancient India is true?
questions.option_1: Each gotra was named after a famous king.
questions.option_2: Women retained their father's gotra after marriage.
questions.option_3: People belonging to the same gotra were regarded as descendants of the person after whom the gotra was named.
questions.option_4: Men and women were expected to marry within the same gotra.
questions.solution:
• Truth: Descendants of a common ancestor
  • Practice: People of the same Gotra were considered siblings; hence, marriage within the same Gotra was forbidden.

questions.question: In the context of Indian Freedom Movement, which of the following years is correctly paired with the event that took place that year?
questions.option_1: 1945 – The All India Congress Committee met in Bombay and ratified the 'Quit India' resolution
questions.option_3: 1915 – Mahatma Gandhi returned from South Africa
questions.option_4: 1944 – The Cripps Mission was sent by the British government to India to obtain Indian cooperation for the British war efforts in the 2nd World War
questions.solution:
• Correct Pair: 1915 – Gandhi returned from South Africa
  • Date: 9 January 1915 (now celebrated as Pravasi Bharatiya Divas).

questions.question: Which of the following varnas was responsible for protecting people and administering justice in ancient India as per rules laid down by the Dharmasutras and Dharmashastras?
questions.solution:
• Varna: Kshatriya
  • Role: According to the Varna system, they were the warrior class meant to protect and rule.

questions.question: Which of the following parties supported the move for partition of Bengal?
questions.solution:
• Party: All India Muslim League
  • Reason: They supported the 1905 partition as it created a Muslim-majority province in East Bengal.

questions.question: Chandannagar was established as a French colony in 1673, obtaining permission from______ the then Nawab of Bengal, to establish a trading post on the right bank of the river Hooghly.
questions.solution:
• Nawab: Ibrahim Khan
  • History: Permission was granted in 1673 to the French East India Company to establish a trading post.

questions.question: With reference to the administration of Delhi Sultanate, which of the following was the department of State Correspondence?
questions.solution:
• Department: Diwan-i-insha
  • Role: Managed all royal correspondence and maintained records of the Sultanate.

questions.question: The Open Hand Monument in Chandigarh was designed by ______.
questions.solution:
• Architect: Le Corbusier
  • Symbolism: The Open Hand symbolizes 'the hand to give and the hand to take; peace and prosperity'.

questions.question: Which of the following events occurred before 1919?
questions.solution:
• Before 1919: Partition of Bengal (1905)
  • Comparison: Chauri Chaura (1922), Lahore Session (1929), Gandhi-Irwin Pact (1931).

questions.question: Which of the following sages of ancient India wrote the ‘Mimamsa-sutras’?
questions.solution:
• Sage: Jaimini
  • Philosophy: The Mimamsa school focuses on the ritualistic interpretation of the Vedas.

questions.question: William Hawkins met Emperor Jahangir as a representative of the ______ East India Company.
questions.solution:
• Company: English East India Company
  • Visit: He visited the court of Jahangir in 1608 to seek trade concessions for the British.

questions.question: In which of the following years was the Mont-Ford Reforms report presented by the British colonial government in India?
questions.solution:
• Year: 1918
  • Context: These reforms led to the Government of India Act 1919, introducing 'Diarchy' in provinces.

questions.question: With which of the following organisations was Lala Har Dayal associated?
questions.solution:
• Party: Ghadar Party
  • Context: Formed in the USA (1913) to overthrow British rule in India through an armed revolution.

questions.question: After the death of Shri Guru Gobind Singh, the Sikhs revolted against the ______ under the leadership of Banda Bahadur.
questions.solution:
• Ruler: Mughals
  • Leader: Banda Singh Bahadur led the Sikh army to avenge the execution of Guru Gobind Singh’s sons.

questions.question: Who among the following leaders of Indian Freedom Movement gave the slogan ‘Freedom is my birthright and I shall have it’?
questions.solution:
• Leader: Bal Gangadhar Tilak
  • Note: Known as 'Lokmanya', he used this slogan to energize the Home Rule Movement.

questions.question: In which of the following forts was Razia Sultan imprisoned by Malik Ikhtiyar-ud-din Altunia?
questions.solution:
• Fort: Qila Mubarak in Bathinda
  • Event: Altunia, the governor of Bathinda, revolted against Razia and imprisoned her there.

questions.question: In which of the following years Motilal Nehru along with eight other congress leaders drafted a Constitution for India?
questions.solution:
• Year: 1928
  • Document: Known as the Nehru Report, it was the first major attempt by Indians to draft a constitution.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs of Indian revolutionaries and organisations is CORRECTLY paired?
questions.option_2: Mahadev Govind Ranade – Madras Mahajana Sabha
questions.option_4: M Veera Raghavachari – Poona Sarvajanik Sabha
questions.solution:
• Correct: Badruddin Tyabji – Bombay Presidency Association
  • Fact: Founded in 1885 by Tyabji, Pherozeshah Mehta, and K.T. Telang.

questions.question: Sikandra is the final resting place of Emperor ______.
questions.solution:
• Location: Akbar
  • Site: Sikandra (Agra) houses the magnificent mausoleum of the third Mughal Emperor.
